item.title: Sr Applied Scientist, Embedded Battery Algorithms, Energy Storage - Amazon.com
item.description:
**DESCRIPTION** ---------------
Do you want to write the algorithms that control next-generation batteries, and shape the future of energy storage? This role sits where electrochemistry, data/ML, and control theory meet. You will develop the physics-informed and data-driven methods that estimate state of charge, health, power capability, and remaining life, and validate them against lab and fleet data until they are ready to ship. Your algorithms will decide how hard a battery can be pushed, when it needs attention, and how long it will last, so they shape the safety, warranty, and economics of the whole product. You will work side by side with cell, systems, and software engineers, and as an early hire you will help define how we develop and validate battery algorithms.
This role can be based in Boston, Irvine, Sunnyvale, or Seattle, and involves occasional domestic and international travel, up to 10% of the time.
Key job responsibilities
* Develop and own algorithms for state of charge, state of health, power capability, and remaining useful life, combining physics-based models with data-driven and estimation methods. * Deliver validated reference implementations, test vectors, and accuracy targets that define what production code must achieve. * Design the test plans and data needed to develop and validate algorithms, working with the cell and testing teams to turn lab and field data into model improvements. * Analyze algorithm performance across the deployed fleet, find where models drift or fail, and drive improvements. * Own the accuracy and robustness of battery algorithms, and sign off that production implementations match the validated reference. Provide algorithm evidence for safety certification.
A day in the life Your week moves between data, models, and experiments. One day you might be working out why a health estimate drifts on cells that have aged in the field, and the next deciding which model structure holds accuracy at cold temperatures. You could be designing a test with the cell team to expose a behavior your model misses, or reviewing an implementation with an applied scientist to confirm that what ships matches what you validated. You will regularly share results with software, systems, and cell leaders, and your findings will shape decisions well beyond the algorithm itself.
About the team We are building Amazon's energy storage capability, providing power for advanced technologies while contributing to a stable grid. Our product is highly connected, yet secure and resilient by design. We own it end to end, from software, ML, and controls through system design to cell selection and supply, and on to a safety-certified product in the field. The organization operates like a startup inside Amazon: small, fast-moving, and accountable for our decisions. We work across hardware, software, and science, with suppliers and partners worldwide, and with Amazon infrastructure, procurement, legal, and finance.
The organization is at an early stage and growing quickly. You will be among the first algorithm hires, so you will help shape how we design, build, certify, and ship, with a direct line of sight to the product and business decisions your work informs. This is a dynamic role that will regularly present new challenges as the product and organization evolve.
**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS** ------------------------
* Master's degree in electrical engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials science, applied mathematics, or a related field. * 8+ years of experience developing battery algorithms or battery models in industry or research with a Master's degree, or 5+ years with a PhD. * Extensive experience launching battery products with leading automotive or grid storage OEMs may be considered in place of some of this experience. * Experience developing state of charge or state of health estimation algorithms for lithium-ion batteries, including building equivalent circuit models and using methods such as Kalman filtering or data-driven models. * Experience validating battery algorithms against laboratory and field data. * Expert proficiency in Python for building and validating battery models, and the ability to prototype algorithms in C. * Familiarity with automotive or battery energy storage system (BESS) safety standards, such as ISO 26262, UL 1973, or UL 9540A.
**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS** ----------------------------
* PhD in electrical engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, materials science, applied mathematics, or a related field. * Experience building physics-based electrochemical models, such as the Doyle-Fuller-Newman (DFN) or single particle model (SPM) or other advanced battery models, and with lithium-ion aging mechanisms. * Experience with lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells, including state of charge estimation across the flat voltage plateau and hysteresis. * Familiarity with lithium-ion failure modes and abuse hazards, such as overcharge, internal short, and thermal runaway, and experience developing algorithms to detect them. * Experience designing battery test protocols, such as hybrid pulse power characterization (HPPC), drive or duty cycles, and impedance spectroscopy. * Experience making technical trade-offs on a safety-critical product, where certification and field reliability constrain cost and schedule. * Comfortable making decisions with incomplete information, and effective across cultures, companies, and time zones.

Amazon Advertising is one of Amazon's fastest growing businesses, responsible for defining and delivering a collection of advertising products that drive discovery and sales.
